ai.literal: Possession of the asset called excellence of the tongue, that excellence is not included in any other excellence.
ai.translation: The possession of the asset called eloquence of the tongue is a unique excellence; that excellence is not to be found among any other excellences.
ai.modern: நாநலம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் நன்மையைப் பெற்றிருப்பது ஒரு சிறந்த உடைமையாகும்; அந்த நன்மை வேறு எந்த நன்மைகளுள்ளும் அடங்குவது அன்று.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of eloquence, termed here as the 'excellence of the tongue' (நாநலம்). The author states that possessing this gift of speech is the greatest asset a person can have. He contrasts it with all other forms of goodness or wealth, asserting that this specific excellence stands completely apart and cannot be matched by any other virtues. The word 'யாநலத்து' refers to any other kind of excellence, emphasizing that eloquence is unparalleled in its power and utility.

ai.literal: And prosperity and ruin by that arising, guarding [against it], avoid slip in speech.
ai.translation: Since both prosperity and ruin arise from one's words, one must guard against carelessness and slips in speech.
ai.modern: ஆக்கமும் அழிவும் ஒருவனுடைய சொல்லினாலேயே உண்டாவதால், தன் சொல்லில் சோர்வு ஏற்படாமல் காத்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the immense power of speech, showing how a person's words can lead to either great prosperity or total ruin. Because words carry such high stakes, one must be extremely vigilant to prevent any careless slips of the tongue. The phrase 'காத்தோம்பல்' highlights the active effort required to maintain control over what one says. Thus, mindful speech is presented as a vital shield for safeguarding one's life and well-being.

ai.literal: Speaking that which has the quality of binding those who listened, and making even those who do not listen desire to hear, is power of speech.
ai.translation: True power of speech lies in speaking such that it captivates those who already listen, and makes even those who do not listen desire to hear.
ai.modern: கேட்டவர்களைத் தன்பால் ஈர்த்துப் பிணித்துக் கொள்ளும் தன்மையுடையதாகவும், கேட்காதவர்களும் விரும்பிக் கேட்கும் படியாகவும் பேசுவதே சொல்வன்மை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate standard of powerful speech (சொல்வன்மை). It must achieve two distinct effects: first, it must bind and captivate those who are already listening ('கேட்டார் பிணிக்கும்'), ensuring they remain engaged. Second, it must be so appealing that even those who are indifferent or disinclined to listen ('கேளாரும்') are moved by a desire ('வேட்ப') to hear it. The poet uses the contrasting terms 'கேட்டார்' (listeners) and 'கேளார்' (non-listeners) to show that a master communicator wins over both friends and strangers alike.

ai.literal: Having understood the suitability, speak the word; virtue and wealth, than that, greater, there is not.
ai.translation: Assess the suitability of the situation and speak your words; there is no greater virtue or wealth than doing so.
ai.modern: தகுதியை அறிந்து சொல்லைச் சொல்ல வேண்டும்; அதைவிடச் சிறந்த அறமும் பொருளும் வேறு இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of speaking with discernment. The word 'tiran' refers to the suitability of the audience, the context, and the manner of delivery. The poet advises us to first understand this suitability before speaking any word. Doing so is of the highest importance, as there is no greater virtue or material benefit than speech delivered with such careful judgment.

ai.literal: Speak the word, having known the absence of another word that conquers that word.
ai.translation: Deliver your speech only after ensuring that no other word can conquer and surpass the words you have chosen.
ai.modern: நீங்கள் பேசும் சொல்லை வெல்லக்கூடிய வேறு ஒரு சொல் இல்லை என்பதை அறிந்து, அச்சொல்லைப் பேசுங்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of choosing unassailable words when speaking. The author advises us to speak a word only after realizing that there is no other word ('பிறிதோர் சொல்') that can conquer ('வெல்லும்') or refute the word we have chosen. By ensuring the non-existence ('இன்மை') of a superior counter-argument or a better-suited term, our speech becomes powerful, flawless, and persuasive.

ai.literal: Speaking themselves so as to make others desire to listen, and grasping the benefit of others' words, is the principle of those who are free from blemish in excellence.
ai.translation: To speak in a way that makes others eager to listen, and to grasp the core essence of what others say, is the practice of those who are free from flaws and rich in excellence.
ai.modern: பிறர் விரும்பிக் கேட்குமாறு தாம் பேசி, பிறர் பேசும் சொற்களின் பயனை ஏற்றுக்கொள்வது, மாண்புகளால் குற்றமற்றவர்களின் கொள்கையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the dual nature of effective communication, which requires both eloquent expression and active listening. A skilled speaker delivers their thoughts in a pleasing manner that naturally attracts the listener's interest. At the same time, they possess the humility and wisdom to listen to others and extract the useful essence from their speech. This balanced practice of speaking agreeably and listening discerningly is the defining principle of noble minds who are free from intellectual or moral flaws.

ai.literal: One who is capable in speaking, who has no slip, and who is fearless—to conquer him in opposition is difficult for anyone.
ai.translation: It is impossible for anyone to defeat in debate a person who is eloquent in speech, free from slips of memory, and completely fearless.
ai.modern: பேசுவதில் வல்லவனாகவும், சோர்வு (மறதி) இல்லாதவனாகவும், அஞ்சாதவனாகவும் இருப்பவனை, விவாதத்தில் வெல்வது எவருக்கும் அரிது.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the three essential qualities that make a speaker invincible in any debate or opposition. First, they must be eloquent and capable of powerful speech ('solalvallan'). Second, they must possess a sharp, alert mind free from slips of memory or confusion ('cōrvilan'). Third, they must be completely fearless ('añcān') when facing opponents. Anyone who possesses this combination of eloquence, mental clarity, and courage cannot be defeated by anyone in an argument.

ai.translation: If the world obtains those who are capable of speaking in a systematic and pleasant manner, it will quickly listen to and carry out their commands.
ai.modern: கருத்துக்களை வரிசையாகவும் இனிமையாகவும் சொல்ல வல்லவர்களைப் பெற்றால், இவ்வுலகம் அவர்கள் ஏவும் கட்டளையை விரைந்து கேட்டுச் செய்யும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the power of effective communication. It states that if the world finds individuals who can present their thoughts in a logical, orderly sequence (நிரந்து) and in a pleasant, agreeable manner (இனிது), it will readily accept their leadership. The world will not only listen to them but will also hasten to execute their commands (தொழில் கேட்கும்). Thus, systematic and sweet speech is the key to gaining influence and authority over others.

ai.literal: To speak many things they will desire, surely, those who have not mastered speaking a few flawless words.
ai.translation: Those who do not know how to speak a few flawless words will surely desire to speak many words.
ai.modern: குற்றமற்ற சில சொற்களைச் சொல்லத் தெரியாதவர்கள், பல சொற்களைப் பேச விரும்புவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the beauty of concise, flawless speech with the tendency of untrained speakers to babble. The phrase 'மாசற்ற சில சொல்லல்' refers to the art of speaking a few words that are completely free of errors or blemishes. Those who have not mastered this art ('தேற்றாதவர்') will surely ('மன்ற') desire ('காமுறுவர்') to speak at great length ('பல சொல்ல'), mistakenly believing that quantity can compensate for a lack of quality.

ai.literal: Even if blooming in clusters, unscented flower-like are they, who what they learned, to be understood, in detail do not speak.
ai.translation: Those who cannot clearly explain what they have learned so that others can understand are like a bunch of flowers that have bloomed but have no fragrance.
ai.modern: தாம் கற்றவற்றை மற்றவர்கள் புரிந்து கொள்ளும்படி விரிவாக எடுத்துச் சொல்ல முடியாதவர்கள், கொத்தாக மலர்ந்திருந்தாலும் மணம் தராத மலரைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of eloquence and communication skills. A person may have acquired vast knowledge through study, but if they cannot articulate it clearly so that others can comprehend it, their learning remains useless. The poet beautifully compares such individuals to a cluster of flowers that, despite blooming abundantly, fail to spread any fragrance.
